root.name: Sicilian Defense: Scheveningen Variation
root.moves: 1. e4 c5 2. Nf3 e6 3. d4 cxd4 4. Nxd4 Nf6 5. Nc3 d6

overview: Black builds the compact ...e6 and ...d6 pawn pair with ...Be7, ...O-O and ...Nc6 or ...a6, and waits to break with ...d5 or ...b5. White's main plans are the English Attack (Be3, f3, Qd2, O-O-O, g4) or the Keres Attack with g4, both for a kingside pawn storm against opposite-side castling. The Classical Be2 and O-O line is quieter. The theory is heavy and Black often has to defend precisely before counterplay arrives.

white_ideas.idea: English Attack: Be3, f3, Qd2, O-O-O and g4-g5 with a pawn storm
Keres Attack 6.g4 to cramp Black's pieces before ...Nc6 or ...h6
Classical Be2, O-O, f4 for a slower kingside build-up

black_ideas.idea: Break with ...d5 or counterplay with ...b5 and ...Rc8 on the c-file

typical_structures.structure: Black e6/d6 pawns against White's e4 pawn with the half-open c-file; Sicilian Scheveningen centre

character.notes: English Attack and Keres Attack mean opposite-side castling and pawn storms where one slip loses fast.

gambit.notes: No material offered in the main lines.

soundness.notes: Sound; Kasparov and Karpov were regular practitioners.

structure.notes: Black has a half-open c-file against e4: semi-open Sicilian.

approach.notes: A main Sicilian branch played at every level, standard.

level.notes: Heavy theory in English Attack lines and subtle plans for Black.
